skills.name: Explain conduction, convection and radiation and their applications

note.text:
Conduction: heat passes through a material from particle to particle, without the material moving as a whole. Metals conduct best because they have free electrons; air, wood, plastic and water are poor conductors (insulators).
Convection: heat is carried by a moving fluid. Warmed fluid expands, becomes less dense and rises; cooler fluid sinks to take its place, making a convection current. It happens only in liquids and gases.
Radiation: heat travels as electromagnetic waves and needs no material medium, so it crosses a vacuum. Dull black surfaces absorb and emit best; shiny light surfaces reflect.
Applications: cooking pots (conduction), heating water from below and ventilation (convection), the Sun's energy and a vacuum flask (radiation).

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to name and explain the three ways heat moves and use them to explain everyday devices.
Builds on: Lesson {1} (heat flows from hot to cold) and Form Two particles and density.
Leads to: Lesson {7} (expansion) and the design of cooking, cooling and solar devices.

sections.heading: Conduction and convection
sections.text:
Conduction: heat passes along a material from particle to particle, while the material itself stays put. The hot particles vibrate more and pass the energy on. In a metal, free electrons carry it much faster, so metals are good conductors. Air, wood, plastic, cloth and water are poor conductors, or insulators.
Convection: in a liquid or a gas, the warmed fluid expands, becomes less dense and rises; cooler, denser fluid sinks to replace it. The circulation is a convection current, and it carries the heat with the moving fluid.
That is why a water heater is placed at the bottom of the tank and the freezer at the top of a refrigerator.

sections.heading: Radiation and applications
sections.text:
Radiation is heat travelling as electromagnetic waves. It needs no material medium, so it crosses the vacuum of space: that is how the Sun's energy reaches us.
• Dull black surfaces are the best absorbers and the best emitters.
• Shiny, light surfaces reflect radiation and are poor emitters.
Uses: solar water-heater pipes are painted dull black to absorb; light clothes are worn in the sun to reflect; a vacuum flask is silvered to reflect radiation, with a vacuum to stop conduction and convection and a stopper to stop evaporation.

key_words.meaning: heat passed from particle to particle in a material
heat carried by a moving fluid
heat travelling as waves, needing no medium

examples: a metal spoon in soup: conduction
a heater at the bottom of a tank: convection
the Sun warming your face: radiation

mistake.wrong: heat from the Sun reaches us by conduction through the air
mistake.why: Space between the Sun and the atmosphere is almost empty: only radiation can cross a vacuum.

worked_example.problem: Explain how a vacuum flask keeps a hot drink hot.
steps: The vacuum between the double walls has no particles, so conduction and convection cannot cross it.
Both glass surfaces are silvered: shiny surfaces are poor emitters and reflect radiation back.
The stopper closes the top, stopping convection and evaporation.
The thin glass walls and the plastic case reduce the little conduction that is left.
worked_example.answer: the vacuum stops conduction and convection; the silvering reflects radiation; the stopper stops evaporation

cards.idea: Conduction passes heat from particle to particle in a solid; metals are best because of their free electrons.
example: a metal spoon in hot soup soon feels hot at the handle; a wooden one does not

cards.idea: Convection carries heat in a moving fluid: warm fluid rises because it is less dense.
example: a heater at the bottom of a tank warms all the water; one at the top does not

cards.idea: Radiation needs no medium and crosses a vacuum; dull black absorbs and emits best.
example: heat from the Sun reaches us through empty space

pick.q: Two cans of hot water are alike except that one is dull black and the other shiny silver. Which cools faster?
pick.r: The dull black one, because a dull black surface is a better emitter of radiation
w: The shiny one, because shiny metal conducts heat away
Both cool at the same rate
The dull black one, because black absorbs more heat
e: The cans are the same metal; the paint changes how well they emit, not how they conduct.
The surfaces differ, so they radiate at different rates.
These cans are hotter than the room, so they are emitting. The answer is right but the reason is not.
pick.y: Both lose heat by conduction and convection alike; the dull black surface emits radiation best.

pick.q: Which surface takes in radiation best?
pick.r: A dull black surface
w: A shiny silver surface
A white painted surface
A polished glass surface
e: A shiny silver surface reflects most of the radiation that falls on it.
White reflects much of the radiation.
Polished glass reflects and lets radiation through rather than absorbing it.
pick.y: A good absorber is also a good emitter: dull black is best at both.

pick.q: Why can radiation reach the Earth from the Sun?
pick.r: Radiation is electromagnetic waves, which need no material medium
w: The air between carries it by conduction
Convection currents cross space
Space is full of particles that pass it along
e: There is almost no matter between the Sun and the atmosphere to conduct through.
Convection needs a fluid to flow; space is very nearly empty.
Space is nearly empty, so there is nothing to pass heat along.
pick.y: Only radiation can cross a vacuum; conduction and convection both need particles.

pick.q: A roof is painted shiny white instead of dull black. What is the effect inside the building?
pick.r: It stays cooler, because the roof reflects more of the Sun's radiation
w: It becomes hotter, because white absorbs more radiation
There is no change, because the roof is the same material
It stays cooler, because white conducts heat away faster
e: Dull dark surfaces absorb best; white reflects.
The surface decides how much radiation is absorbed, whatever the material beneath.
The colour changes how much radiation is absorbed, not how well the roof conducts.
pick.y: Shiny light surfaces reflect radiation, so less of the Sun's energy enters the building.

pick.q: A metal spoon left in hot soup becomes hot at the handle. Which method of heat transfer is this?
pick.r: Conduction
w: Convection
Radiation
Evaporation
e: Convection needs a fluid to move; the spoon is solid and stays still.
Radiation needs no contact, but here the heat travels through the metal itself.
Evaporation is a change of state at a liquid surface, not a way of carrying heat along a spoon.
pick.y: In a solid, heat passes from particle to particle and, in a metal, by free electrons: that is conduction.

pick.q: Why is the heating element of a water heater placed near the bottom of the tank?
pick.r: So that the warm water rises and sets up a convection current
w: So that the heat can radiate upwards
Because heat cannot travel downwards at all
To keep the element away from the steam
e: Radiation travels in all directions and is not the main effect in water.
Heat can travel downwards by conduction and radiation; the point is that warm water rises.
Keeping it away from steam is not the reason for heating from below.
pick.y: Warm water expands, becomes less dense and rises, while cooler water sinks to take its place: a convection current heats the whole tank.

pick.q: Which surface is the best absorber and emitter of radiation?
pick.r: A dull black surface
w: A shiny silver surface
A white painted surface
All surfaces are equally good
e: A shiny silver surface reflects radiation and is a poor absorber and emitter.
White reflects much of the radiation that falls on it.
Colour and texture change how well a surface absorbs and emits.
pick.y: Dull black surfaces absorb and emit radiation best; shiny, light surfaces reflect it.

pick.q: How does heat from the Sun reach the Earth?
pick.r: By radiation, which needs no material medium
w: By conduction through the air
By convection currents in space
By all three methods equally
e: There is almost no matter between the Sun and the atmosphere to conduct through.
Convection needs a fluid to move; space is very nearly empty.
Only one of the three can cross a vacuum, so they are not equal here.
pick.y: Radiation is electromagnetic waves, so it can cross a vacuum. Conduction and convection cannot.

pick.q: Why is a vacuum flask silvered on both sides of the double wall?
pick.r: To reflect radiation back, so little heat enters or leaves
w: To stop conduction through the glass
To make the flask look attractive
To stop convection inside the liquid
e: Conduction is stopped by the vacuum between the walls, not by the silvering.
The appearance is not the reason; the silvering is inside the double wall.
Convection inside the liquid is not what the silvering prevents.
pick.y: Shiny silver surfaces are poor emitters and good reflectors, so radiation is turned back.

pick.q: Why does warm water rise in a convection current?
pick.r: It expands, so the same mass fills a larger volume and its density falls
w: Warm water is heavier than cold water
Heat always travels upwards
The water is pushed up by the heater
e: Warming expands water, so it becomes LESS dense, not heavier.
Heat travels in all directions; here it is the moving fluid that carries it upwards.
The heater does not push the water; the difference in density does.
pick.y: Density = mass ÷ volume, and less dense fluid floats above denser fluid.

pick.q: In which materials can convection carry heat?
pick.r: Only in liquids and gases, because the material itself must move
w: In solids, liquids and gases alike
Only in solids
Only in a vacuum
e: The particles of a solid are held in place, so they cannot carry heat across the body.
Convection needs a fluid that can flow, which a solid cannot do.
A vacuum has no particles at all; only radiation crosses it.
pick.y: Convection moves heat by moving the fluid itself, so it needs a liquid or a gas.

pick.q: Why is the cooling unit of a refrigerator placed at the top?
pick.r: Air cooled at the top becomes denser and sinks, cooling the whole cabinet
w: Cold air rises, so it must start at the top
The food at the top needs the most cooling
There is no room for it at the bottom
e: Cold air is denser than warm air, so it sinks.
All the food needs cooling; the placing is about the circulation.
The placing is chosen for the convection current, not for space.
pick.y: Cooled air sinks and warmer air rises to be cooled, so a current circulates through the fridge.

pick.q: Smoke is held over one chimney of a box with two chimneys and a candle under the other. What is seen, and why?
pick.r: The smoke is drawn down one chimney and out of the other, showing a convection current
w: The smoke rises straight up from both chimneys
The smoke stays still above the box
The smoke is blown away from the box
e: Air leaves above the candle, so smoke cannot rise from that chimney.
The candle sets the air moving, so the smoke does move.
Nothing blows the smoke away; the current pulls it in.
pick.y: Warm air above the candle rises and leaves, so cooler air (with the smoke) is drawn down the other chimney.

pick.q: are cooking pots usually made of metal with wooden or plastic handles
pick.r: Metal conducts heat quickly to the food, while wood and plastic are poor conductors and stay cool to hold
pick.w2: Wood radiates heat better than metal
pick.w3: Plastic conducts heat faster than metal
pick.y: A good conductor carries heat to the food; a poor conductor keeps the handle safe to touch.

pick.q: do people wear light-coloured clothes in hot sunshine
pick.r: Light surfaces reflect much of the radiation instead of absorbing it
pick.w2: Light colours conduct heat away faster
pick.y: A dull dark surface absorbs radiation best, so light colours keep the wearer cooler.

pick.q: is the freezer compartment placed at the top of a refrigerator
pick.r: Air cooled at the top sinks, setting up a convection current that cools the whole fridge
pick.w1: Cold air rises to the top
pick.w2: The motor is at the bottom
pick.w3: Food at the top spoils faster
pick.y: Cooled air becomes denser and sinks, while warmer air rises to be cooled.

pick.q: are the pipes of a solar water heater painted dull black
pick.r: A dull black surface absorbs radiation from the Sun better than a shiny one
pick.w1: Black paint conducts heat better than metal
pick.w3: Black paint stops convection in the water
pick.y: The pipes must take in as much of the Sun's radiation as possible, and dull black absorbs best.

pick.q: does a room need vents near the ceiling and near the floor
pick.r: Warm stale air leaves at the top while cool fresh air enters at the bottom: a convection current
pick.w1: Radiation can only pass through high openings
pick.w2: Heat is conducted out through the vents
pick.w3: Two vents simply make the room brighter
pick.y: Warm air rises and leaves through the upper vent, drawing cooler air in at the bottom.

pick.q: Put the parts of a vacuum flask in order, from the inside outwards.
s: The liquid is held in a double-walled glass vessel
Both glass surfaces facing the gap are silvered, so radiation is reflected back
The space between the walls is a vacuum, so there are no particles to conduct or convect
A stopper closes the top to stop convection and evaporation
A plastic or metal case protects the glass

pick.q: Put the stages of a convection current in a tank of water in order.
s: The heater at the bottom warms the water near it
That water expands, so the same mass fills a larger volume
Its density falls below that of the water above it
The warm water rises and cooler, denser water sinks to take its place
The circulation carries heat through the whole tank

pick.q: Put the stages by which the Sun's energy heats water in a solar heater in order.
s: Radiation from the Sun crosses the empty space and the atmosphere
It falls on the dull black pipes, which are good absorbers
The pipes become hot and conduct heat to the water touching them
The warmed water rises to the tank above by convection
Cooler water flows down to the pipes and is heated in turn
